subject: Tactical MAP lockstep: security acceptance & data-retention annex

Subject: Tactical MAP lockstep: security acceptance & data-retention annex

Anna / Security team —

Thanks for the time last week. Attached is a first-draft MAP (redwood-map-v1.xlsx) that aligns evaluation sprints to the security/compliance gates you flagged: SOC 2 evidence, SIG/CAIQ responses, DPA negotiation, and explicit data-retention windows for model artifacts & logs. High-level proposal:

- Week 1 (Sep 1–7): Evidence intake & CAIQ Q&A; DPA redline exchange
- Week 2 (Sep 8–14): Evidence verification & technical walkthrough (embeddings/logging/residency)
- Week 3 (Sep 15–21): Final DPA sign-off and mutual acceptance — MAP close

Key asks from Mercury: SOC 2 Type II (or Redwood SOC2 summary + attestation stub), completed CAIQ, and DPA carveouts for archival/residency. We call out two gating moments in the MAP:

1) Technical Acceptance Gate — SOC2 summary + CAIQ answers + confirmation of encryption/residency (required to move to a dedicated pilot)
2) Legal Acceptance Gate — Countersigned DPA (or mutually agreed redline) for production enablement

Please review the MAP and the provisional retention table in the sheet labeled "Retention Annex". Specific items we need from you:
- Which retention windows (logs, request bodies, embeddings, model artifacts) are acceptable per your policy team?
- Any mandatory CAIQ sections you want prioritized?
- Preferred date for a security + legal sync (we propose Tue 2026-09-08 10:00 PT).

Attached: redwood-map-v1.xlsx (MAP + retention annex). I can also export a one-pager if you prefer.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Kim —

Appreciate the clear plan and the retention annex. Quick notes from Security/Legal triage after an initial read:

- SOC 2: We need a Type II report if available. If you don't have that publicly, a concise SOC2 summary + control-owner evidence (passwords, key rotation cadence, encryption at rest KMS info) will suffice for the MAP Gate 1 intake.
- CAIQ: We will send a prioritized CAIQ template this afternoon (we prefer answers inline in the spreadsheet).
- DPA: Our legal team prefers a DPA redline rather than reauthoring from scratch. We'll return a redline with comments on data-subject rights and subprocessors (notably: clarify any subprocessor in APAC).
- Retention: Primary ask — explicitly list retention for (1) request payloads, (2) embeddings, (3) KV caches, (4) audit logs. Please confirm whether embeddings are stored encrypted and whether they are purged on customer request.

We can do Tue 2026-09-08 10:00 PT for Security + Legal. I'll include our lead counsel and product-security.

I'm attaching a short list of SIG/CAIQ questions we want prioritized: mercury_sig_questions.xlsx (see top 10). We'll return with DPA redline by COB Sep 6.

Best,
Anna Brown
Senior Security Manager, MercuryBank
anna.brown@mercurybank.com

Forwarding Anna's note. We need an internal owner for each intake item and a short deliverable plan to keep the MAP on the proposed sprint. Proposed owners:

- SOC2 evidence & summary (owner: Neha) — target deliverable: soc2-summary-stub.pdf + control-owner contacts by EOD Sep 6

Acceptance gating: once SOC2 summary + CAIQ answers are in and technical clarifications accepted in the scheduled sync, we mark Technical Acceptance Gate satisfied. DPA countersignature remains Legal Acceptance Gate.

Can each of you reply with a one-line ack and any schedule conflicts. Marcus — you'll need to prepare a short note on embeddings lifecycle & deletion API behavior (Anna asked explicitly).

Thanks —
Kim
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Anna Brown <anna.brown@mercurybank.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tactical MAP lockstep: security acceptance & data-retention annex

Anna / Kimberly / team —

Quick technical clarifications to land the retention annex before the sync:

- Embeddings: stored encrypted at rest (AES-256) and scoped per customer. Embedding vectors are retained by default for 30 days in the hosted flow; for dedicated/private we can set retention per contract. We expose a deletion API that removes embeddings from the active index and schedules secure purge from cold storage within 72 hours.
- KV cache: ephemeral per-request by default (max TTL 2 hours); we offer an optional session cache for dedicated pools with configurable TTL — we can scope TTL in the retention annex.
- Request payloads / prompt text: stored for 14 days by default for debugging; can be shortened or disabled for enterprise customers.
- Audit logs: retained for 365 days (configurable). We can provide filtered export (CSV) for compliance reviews.
- Residency: primary region for Mercury will be us-west-2; subprocessors in EU/APAC are documented in the subprocessor registry and we will highlight any APAC processors in the DPA redline.

I've attached the soc2-summary-stub.pdf which pulls together control owners and a short evidence checklist for intake. I'll join the Tue 9/8 sync and prepare a 10-minute walkthrough of embedding lifecycle and key config knobs.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
